newsitem.title: USA: President Clinton to have surgery - doctors.
newsitem.headline: President Clinton to have surgery - doctors.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will have to undergo surgery to repair a torn tendon in his upper right thigh after a late-night fall, doctors said on Friday.
Clinton will have surgery at Bethesda Naval Hospital once he returns to Washington from Florida where he was on a fundraising visit on Thursday.
Clinton hurt his leg and right knee when he fell on some steps in the middle of the night at the estate of golfer Greg Norman, where the president was staying.
Doctors at St Mary's Hospital in West Palm Beach where Clinton was taken for X-rays, said his leg was in a splint and the president was likely to be on crutches for a few weeks.

"He has a tear in the quadricep tendon," Dr. Joel Cohen said at a press briefing. "It's not an uncommon injury. The expectation would be a return to full activity. They're going to sew the tendon back to his kneecap. He literally pulled the tenon from the bone," she said.
Clinton is due to meet Russian President Boris Yeltsin in Helsinki on March 19 for talks on NATO expansion and other matters. There was no comment on whether the summit would be affected.
